Let's start with some of the fundamentals around React Native and React in particular, starting with virtual DOM. How would you define the concept of virtual DOM in React Native?
conversation.candidate: OK, virtual DOM. DOM stands for Document Object Model. It's basically a tree-like structure for the HTML element. Whenever we do any update in our component, the whole tree gets updated, and the whole CSS will recalculate, and the whole UI needs to be updated. Virtual DOM is just a copy of the real DOM. Whenever we do any changes in our file, those changes first get reflected to the virtual DOM. After that, the virtual DOM and real DOM get compared using a diffing algorithm, and only the changes are reflected to the real DOM. Not the whole tree gets updated, and not the whole CSS will recalculate. This is the advantage of using the virtual DOM.

conversation.interviewer: How do you take care of the lifecycle of a functional component? Like how do you take care of mounting, unmounting, and updating?
conversation.candidate: Each component has some lifecycle like mounting. Mounting means the first time our component loads on the screen. In the case of a functional component, to achieve the lifecycle method, we use the useEffect hook. The syntax of useEffect is like the first argument is the callback function, and the second argument is the array of dependencies. If the array of dependencies is empty, then that effect will run as a component didMount. If we pass any state or props in that array of dependencies, then that effect will run when that state or prop value changes. It will work as a component didUpdate. For componentWillUnmount, we can do some cleanup operations to avoid memory leaks by using the return statement inside useEffect.

conversation.interviewer: There are two other hooks as well, right? There is a hook called useCallback and useMemo. Explain.
conversation.candidate: Suppose I have created a functional component. Inside that component, I have written some function. Whenever my component re-renders, that function will recreate each time, leading to performance issues. To avoid this, we can wrap our function in useCallback. The first argument is the function we want to wrap, and the second argument is the array of dependencies. If the array of dependencies is empty, that function will create only at the first time, at the mounting phase. If we pass any state or prop value in that array of dependencies, then if that state or prop changes, only then will that function recreate. UseMemo has the same syntax. If I'm doing some heavy calculation, I can wrap that calculation in useMemo to avoid recalculating each time the component re-renders.
